subject: FinLedger — urgent: queueing & throughput gap on reserved capacity

Subject: High error rate & timeouts — Redwood Dedicated (DL-7621)

Hi Rachel,

We're seeing a sustained spike in inference timeouts and 5xx errors across our production workload starting ~08:10 PST. Latency for short responses has jumped from ~120ms to >2s, and about 12% of requests are failing with 504/502. This is on our reserved Dedicated pool (contract DL-7621).

Impact: our payment flows are timing out and customers are getting retries. This is partially causing increased error rates in our telemetry and is materially impacting our SLAs. Can you confirm whether this is a Redwood side issue (pool saturation / routing) or something on our end?

We've attached a small sample of request traces and SDK logs. Please escalate as needed — this is P1 for us.

Attachments: finledger_early_trace.txt (log snippet), client_sdk_ids.csv

Thanks,
Laura Chen

Subject: FW: High error rate & timeouts — Redwood Dedicated (DL-7621) — internal

Internal — copying the ticket and initial customer notes. Summary of what I'm seeing from quick checks:
- Dedicated pool ded-pool-7 in us-west-2 is at sustained 98% GPU utilization starting 08:05 PST.
- Per-node queuing has increased, and our KV cache hit rate dropped due to a burst of long-context requests.
- Reserved throughput (committed RPS in contract DL-7621) is not being met because other tenants in the same regional placement are consuming burst credits and our autoscaler did not react quickly enough.

Immediate asks:
- Neha: please open emergency autoscale override for FinLedger's pool and confirm what burst capacity we can provision within 15 min.
- Marissa: contact infra/runtime on-call to check for stragglers and reclaim any idle allocations in the pool; request preemption window if possible.
- Vivek: FYI / please prep an escalation note for sales leadership in case the customer wants contract remedies.

Attachments: reserved_capacity_report.csv (current utilization snapshot)

I'll join the triage with FinLedger at 09:35.

— Rachel

Subject: Escalation: FinLedger reserved capacity shortfall — potential SLA impact

Team — quick summary for leadership:
- Customer: FinLedger (DL-7621) — production latency and error-rate spike observed 08:05–09:45 PST.
- Root cause (preliminary): regional dedicated pool saturation (ded-pool-7) and slower-than-expected autoscale reaction; additional contribution from a sudden burst of long-context batch traffic.
- Customer impact: payment flows timing out; business-critical.

Recommended immediate actions:
1) Allocate emergency burst capacity to FinLedger's pool (Neha: confirm delta and ETA).
2) Temporarily reroute FinLedger reads to our adjacent pool (cross-region fallback) while we stabilize.
3) Offer a short-term SLA remedy/credits if latency SLAs were missed; finance ops to prepare options.
4) Post-mortem within 48 hours with capacity gating/placement changes.

I've attached the mutual action plan link and current utilization snapshot. We should aim to have a stabilization update to the customer within 4 hours.

Attachments: https://redwood.app/s/MAP-4982, reserved_capacity_report.csv

— Jonas
VP, Infrastructure Operations
From: Rachel Kim <rachel@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Chen <laura@finledger.com>, Timothy Rhodes <tim.rhodes@finledger.com>
Cc: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 16 Jun 2026 17:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Update & next steps — FinLedger incident 2026-06-14

Hi Laura / Tim,

Thanks again for your patience while we investigated. Summary of findings and actions taken:

Findings:
- The spike was driven by a misconfigured internal FinLedger nightly job that began issuing long-context inference requests at a high rate shortly before 08:05 PST on 2026-06-14. The job's traffic pattern amplified queuing in ded-pool-7 and consumed burst credits intended for short bursts.
- Our autoscale did not provision within the customer's committed SLA window because the pattern resembled steady load initially; we have a tuning action below.

Immediate remediations we performed:
- Routed FinLedger traffic to adjacent burst pool temporarily and increased their dedicated autoscale delta to restore headroom within 10 minutes.
- Applied per-customer rate shaping to prevent single-job exhaustion of burst credits while we worked on a longer-term fix.
- Prioritized FinLedger's placement for the next 72 hours to avoid recurrence during their peak windows.

Next steps (agreed action items):
1) FinLedger: update the nightly job to respect the SDK concurrency cap (we can share suggested settings).
2) Redwood: deliver a short runbook for on-call to quickly identify similar job-driven spikes and a capacity tuning change for autoscale thresholds (owner: Neha).
3) We'll run a joint test next Tuesday to verify the new config and placement.

We've attached an action plan and the utilization snapshot. As a goodwill gesture, we'll apply a credit for affected inference requests during the incident window; our finance team will follow up with a formal credit note.

Attachments: action_plan.pdf, reserved_capacity_report.csv
Links: https://redwood.app/s/MAP-4982

If you'd like, we can schedule a 30-min technical sync tomorrow to walk through the runbook and config changes.

Regards,
Rachel Kim
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
